claim_text: The test suite is green (52 tests pass).
Fixture agent records 12 steps alternating llm_call/tool_call; replay-from-cache 0 LLM calls; substitution dirty-set 5 LLM re-execs; bisect 4 probes 0 LLM calls.
Record overhead per LLM call < 5 ms p99 (README §Performance targets).
The .sb HMAC chain detects tampering and Ed25519 verifier accepts untouched files (README §trace file format).
Trace size on disk < 30% of raw LLM payload bytes (CBOR + gzip + per-message dedup against header dictionary).
Repository layout matches README §Repository layout (planned): stepback/{recorder,replay,substitutions,trace,cli,tui}/ as packages, plus ts/, server/, examples/, docs/.
Each frame is a length-prefixed CBOR object (README §trace file format).
Replay of an unchanged 200-step trace from cache < 2 s end-to-end on a laptop, zero LLM calls.
Bisect of a 200-step trace ≤ 10 probes, ≤ 5 s wall, zero LLM calls.
Substitution of one step in a 200-step trace typically ≤ 10 real LLM re-executions (dirty-set size).
v0.1 target: Python SDK covering OpenAI + Anthropic clients and the LangChain tool registry.
Recorder shims for Anthropic / Bedrock / vLLM LLM clients.
Tool-registry shims for LangChain / CrewAI / AutoGen / MCP.
TypeScript SDK exists (ts/ directory).
Optional team-tier hosted replay engine (server/).
Five worked use-case examples in examples/ (01-bisect-bad-payment.md … 05-regulator-replay-under-new-policy.md).
Textual-based interactive TUI (`stepback inspect` interactive timeline + step viewer).
Web UI for the team tier.
`stepback verify --policy-changed-since` re-executes a trace under a newer toolwarden policy version and emits a structured report.
stepback depends on the same auditable-controller-core package toolwarden uses (shared verified append-only-log implementation).
stepback verify produces a signed Ed25519 attestation pack (regulator-replay tier, m8).
step_kind enumerates llm_call | tool_call | router | parallel_branch_open | parallel_branch_join | exception (parallel-branch + router step kinds).
nondeterminism_hash captures system clock reads, RNG draws, env vars, network responses as a divergence detector.
cost_usd is computed from usage × price-list version pinned in the trace header.
compare_branches produces a step-by-step diff: output diffs, decision changes, cost deltas, and which steps diverged from cache.
Cache hit rate for counterfactual policy audits is typically > 99%.

Pre-existing tools (LangSmith, LangFuse, Phoenix, Helicone, PromptLayer, TruLens, pytest-vcr, MS Agent Governance Toolkit, rr, Pernosco, airportyh/time-traveling-debugger, Sentry/Datadog APM) all fail the 'record + branch + substitute + cached partial replay' test (README §Why nothing else fills this gap).
trace_writer.py docstring: gzip+blob-dedup is the implementation of README's '<30% of raw LLM payload bytes' Performance target.
report.py docstring: 'deterministic and content-addressable so two engineers reading the same trace + substitutions get byte-identical reports' (rendered Markdown reports are byte-stable).
branch_io.py docstring: 'a counterfactual can never silently bind to a different recorded run' — load_branch raises BranchTraceMismatch on tampered traces.
shims.py docstring: wrap_openai / wrap_anthropic / wrap_langchain_tool / wrap_mcp_session are 'drop-in wrappers around the real client objects' usable in production by 'swapping one constructor'.
shims.py docstring: each wrap_* helper 'works against any object whose method shape matches the reference SDKs as of the dates pinned in stepback/pricing.py'.
report.py docstring: 'The CLI subcommand stepback report TRACE [--substitute SPEC ...] [--branch FILE] [--baseline-branch FILE] [-o OUT.md] is wired in stepback.cli'.

trace_writer.py docstring: 'A blob frame is only emitted when a given sub-tree is referenced at least DEFAULT_BLOB_MIN_REUSE times — otherwise the per-blob HMAC wrapper overhead (~280 bytes) would outweigh the saving.'
GROUNDING.md row 13: 'compressed .sb is 61.7% of raw payload bytes ... a large reduction (69.9%) vs the uncompressed .sb' — direct refutation of <30% target preserved as audit evidence.
stepback/pricing.py docstring claim that 'Prices … taken from published lists as of SNAPSHOT_DATE'.

Recorder.parallel() docstring: 'Sequential execution today; the on-disk frames are explicitly marked parallel so a future scheduler can re-execute branches concurrently without changing the trace shape.'

trace_writer.py docstring decomposition: 'gzip catches local redundancy inside one step, and the reuse-aware blob table catches cross-step duplication of recurring objects' — i.e. each compression mechanism is responsible for a distinct, measurable share of the saving.
shims.py: 'The Anthropic response shape is *canonicalised* into the OpenAI {"choices":[...],"usage":{...}} shape so cost accounting and replay semantics are uniform across providers.'
shims.py wrap_openai: returned OpenAIChatCompletion namespace mirrors SDK fields including 'choices[i].message.tool_calls' and 'choices[i].finish_reason' (not just .content / .usage).
shims.py: 'canonicalisation runs on both sides so a cache hit is bit-identical' — i.e. record-time canonical form == replay-time canonical form, byte-for-byte.

stepback/__init__.py exports add 15 new public symbols from shims (wrap_openai/anthropic/langchain_tool/langchain_tools/mcp_session, executors, wrapped classes) — the v0.1 public surface is now what the README §Status target line names.

pricing.py new public surface (aggregate_costs, check_budget, diff_costs, snapshot_age_days, BudgetCheck, format_usd, set_strict, MissingPriceError) is grounded by 31 test cases — but the docstring's 'Step-record contract' shape (specific keys step_id/step_kind/model/usage/cost_usd) has no schema-validation test pinning that records lacking these keys are 'silently treated as no-cost steps'.

Recorder.parallel() join inputs claim: 'a substitution inside any branch propagates dirtiness through the join (and only through the join — sibling branches stay cached).' The 'only through the join — sibling branches stay cached' half is not directly asserted by an existing test (test_branch_dirty_count_strictly_less_than_serial measures aggregate dirty count, not per-sibling cache state).

GROUNDING.md row 23: 'tests/test_e2e_replay.py gained 5 numeric-threshold tests pinning trace-size bounds, replay-vs-record wall-clock speedup, model-substitution cost drop > 1%, bisect probe-count <= ceil(log2 N)+1 (<=5 for the 12-step fixture), and a CLI bisect smoke.' — diff shows only 4 NEW tests in test_e2e_replay.py (HEAD~1 had 14 def test_, HEAD has 18); test_cli_bisect_finds_step pre-existed at HEAD~1 line 272 and is not new.

test_e2e_replay.py::test_replay_speedup_vs_record_is_measurable docstring: 'Cached replay must be measurably faster than fresh record. ... wall-clock under the recorder time'. The actual assertion is `replay_time < record_time * 2.0 + 0.05` which permits replay to be up to ~2x SLOWER than record (plus 50ms slack) — it cannot prove a speedup, only an upper bound on slowdown.

test_parallel_branches.py::test_zero_llm_replay_speedup_vs_record docstring: 'Cached replay must be measurably faster than fresh record... replay of an 11-step trace must take less wall-clock time than recording it.' Same shape as the e2e_replay twin: assertion `replay_time < record_time * 2.0 + 0.05` allows ~2x slowdown, not a speedup.

GROUNDING.md row 24: 'tests/test_parallel_branches.py ... replay wall-clock <= 2x record.' This row faithfully restates the assertion (which is what the test pins), but the language wraps the same speedup framing as row 23 — should be paired with a tightened test that actually shows replay < record before being treated as a speedup guarantee.

GROUNDING.md row 22: 'The full test suite is now green at 132 tests (up from 108 in row 11; +24 numeric-threshold guarantees added across compression, pricing, parallel-branches, e2e-replay, branch-io).' — pytest count 132 verified by command; per-file deltas e2e=+4, parallel=+6, compression=+3, pricing=+5, branch_io=+6 = +24 confirmed.

GROUNDING.md row 25: 'tests/test_compression.py grew 9 -> 12 tests, adding (a) blob-digest tamper detection independent of HMAC, (b) header advertises compression/blob_threshold/blob_min_reuse, (c) absolute-size ceiling: a 60-step chat-history compressed .sb is < 200 KB, uncompressed dominates compressed by >= 2x, per-step compressed cost < 3.5 KB.' Items (a) and (b) actually pre-existed in HEAD~1 (test_blob_digest_tamper_detection and test_header_advertises_compression_scheme were already in tests/test_compression.py); only the 60-step chat-history numeric-threshold test (and 2 others) are new in HEAD.

GROUNDING.md row 30: 'fan-out fixture ... records exactly 11 steps with kind counts llm_call=5, tool_call=4, parallel_branch_open=1, parallel_branch_join=1, and a ToolOutputSubstitution inside one branch dirties exactly 3 steps.' Verified: test_recorded_trace_numeric_bounds asserts those exact kind counts, and test_dirty_subtree_is_small_fraction asserts dirty == 3.

GROUNDING.md row 28: 'cached-prompt-token discount on gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 matches OpenAI's published 4x ratio.' Inline command output `ratio=4.000` matches; test_cached_token_savings_ratio_bounded pins [3.9, 5.0]. The CLAIM that this is OpenAI's published 4x ratio is grounded against the test value, but no citation URL to OpenAI's price page is committed alongside (so 'matches OpenAI's published' is asserted, not verified against an upstream artefact).

GROUNDING.md row 29: 'Bisect on the 12-step fixture finds the bad step in <= ceil(log2 12)+1 = 5 probes with zero LLM re-executions.' Bench output `bisect_probes=4 bisect_llm_calls=0 bad_step=step:12` matches; test_bisect_probe_count_is_logarithmic asserts the same upper bound. Grounded.

GROUNDING.md row 31: '.sbb branch files are tiny by construction: a single-substitution branch is between 50 B and 4 KB and < 50% of the base-trace size. Round-trip preserves count for all 5 substitution kinds.' Verified by test_sbb_branch_file_size_bounded + test_save_branch_substitution_count_matches_loaded.

GROUNDING.md row 32: 'trace-writer header now advertises the compression scheme metadata: compression == COMPRESSION_SCHEME (=gzip+dedup-2) and blob_threshold/blob_min_reuse are present in every .sb written with compression=True.' Inline reproducer command emits `compression=gzip+dedup-2 bt=200 bmr=2 expected=gzip+dedup-2 bt_def=200 bmr_def=2`. Grounded.
GROUNDING.md row 27: 'tests/test_branch_io_and_cli.py grew to 27 tests with 6 new numeric-threshold guarantees.' Verified per-file delta = +6 (HEAD~1 21 -> HEAD 27).

GROUNDING.md row 26: 'tests/test_pricing.py grew 26 -> 31 tests. Notable additions: cached-token discount bounded between 3.9x and 5.0x; diff_costs __total__ strictly equals sum of per-model deltas; RATE_TABLE/PRICE_LIST >= 10 entries and every alias resolves into RATE_TABLE.' All three additions match committed test bodies; per-file delta confirmed +5.

tests/test_e2e_replay.py::test_model_substitution_cost_drop_is_significant comment: 'mini is ~30x cheaper for the substituted step; even with only 1/6 LLM steps swapped the savings dwarf 1%.' The test only asserts `drop_ratio > 0.01` (>1%); the '~30x' multiplier and '1/6 LLM steps' framing are not pinned by any assertion or GROUNDING row that prints the actual per-model rate ratio for gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 vs the recorded baseline.
Severity bands map score thresholds <10→info, <25→low, <50→medium, <75→high, >=75→critical (stepback/report.py SeverityScore docstring L746).
render_html_report emits a self-contained HTML report with NO JavaScript and NO remote assets — inline CSS only (stepback/report.py render_html_report docstring).
_llm_decision_signature is robust to non-conforming OpenAI-shape outputs — it swallows KeyError/IndexError/TypeError and returns (None, None) without raising (stepback/report.py L774).
_depth_of has a cycle / pathological guard at depth > 10_000 that prevents infinite recursion on cyclic parent_step_id graphs (stepback/report.py L811).
CLI --output extension inference (_infer_format_from_path) accepts .htm and .markdown extensions in addition to .html/.json/.md (stepback/cli.py _infer_format_from_path).
SeverityScore.to_dict rounds component floats to 6 decimal places (stepback/report.py SeverityScore.to_dict L759).

severity_score populates a 'reasons' list with one human-readable string per non-zero contributing axis (cost/dirty/decision_flips/subtree_depth) on a real counterfactual (stepback/report.py L888-898).
CLI --format md continues to be accepted as an alias of markdown after the format-dispatcher refactor (stepback/cli.py p_report.add_argument choices include 'md').

tests/test_shims.py::test_openai_replay_real_vs_cached_call_counts docstring (HEAD b601985): a single-prompt substitution dirties exactly 2 of N steps. The actual assertion is assert dirty == n_calls (i.e. ALL N steps dirty, full propagation through the chain) and the inline comment 5 lines later contradicts the docstring. The docstring claim of 2 of N is false against the test body.

tests/test_shims.py::test_anthropic_recorded_cost_per_token_within_bounds docstring (HEAD b601985): Pins that pricing.PRICE_LIST is wired up and consulted on the recording path for Anthropic models. The test only asserts cost_usd is in (0, 0.01) and per-token < 1e-3. That bound is also satisfied by any hardcoded pricing constant; the test does not assert recorded cost == compute_cost(model, usage) using PRICE_LIST.

GROUNDING.md row 53 (HEAD b601985): marginal per-substitution overhead approx 126 B (well inside the test 20 < marginal < 256 envelope). The 126 B observation is from one inline command run; the test pinned envelope is the wide [20, 256] range, so a regression that doubles per-sub overhead to ~250 B would still pass. The narrow around 126 B claim is not pinned.

GROUNDING.md row 49 / tests/test_compression.py::test_compression_dedup_scales_sublinearly (HEAD b601985): dedup quality strictly improves (delta approx -0.12) at larger scale. The test asserts ratio60 <= ratio20 + 0.05 which permits ratio60 to be UP TO 0.05 LARGER than ratio20 — i.e. allows dedup to slightly REGRESS, not strictly improve. The strict improvement framing in the row is stronger than what the test pins.

tests/test_branch_io_and_cli.py::test_cli_inspect_per_step_json_size_bounded (HEAD b601985): comment claims Empirically ~600-2000 B/step but the assertion 100 < per_step < 4000 permits 100-4000 B/step, a band 4x wider on the upper side than the empirically-observed ceiling. A regression doubling per-step JSON to 3500 B would slip past.

tests/test_parallel_branches.py::test_branch_names_uniqueness_and_count (HEAD b601985): assertion names == sorted(names) or set(names) == {research/t for t in FACTS} is logically loose — if set(names) matches, the sortedness branch is short-circuited. The sorted half of the disjunction (a determinism guarantee) is therefore not actually enforced when the set membership matches.

tests/test_branch_io_and_cli.py::test_cli_replay_forced_step_outputs_match_substitution (HEAD b601985): the forced step actually carries the substituted payload bytes — pins that the substitution did not get silently dropped. The test asserts dirty/cache counts and that step:2 is dirty IF the dirty field is present (the inner if dirty in by_id[step:2] makes the strongest assertion conditional). The actual substituted PAYLOAD bytes (LOOKUP_FIXED_ROW content) are NEVER compared against any field in the JSON output.

GROUNDING.md row 47 (HEAD b601985): 162 tests (up from 150 in row 33; +12 new numeric-threshold tests). Per-file deltas in row 47 sum to: branch_io +4, compression +1, parallel_branches +3, shims +4 = 12. Total claim 150 -> 162 = +12 matches.

stepback/attestation.py L19-43 docstring 'On-disk shape (canonical JSON, no embedded binary)' enumerates pack JSON fields including 'magic':'stepback/.pack', 'format_version':1, 'summary.replayed_ok', 'summary.divergent_traces', 'summary.total_cost_delta_usd', 'policy_version_pin', 'body_hash':'sha256:<hex>', 'signature':'ed25519:<hex>'. GROUNDING row 68 emits only pack_bytes, entries, verify=ok and does not pin any of these schema-field names or the magic/format_version constants.

stepback/attestation.py L40-43 docstring claim 'Verification is *strictly* offline: the auditor needs only the attestor public key — no .sb traces, no Python source, no policy file.' GROUNDING row 68 verifies a pack but uses the same process that wrote it, with the .sb fixture and Python source in scope; no row demonstrates verify_attestation_pack succeeding when only the .pack file + attestor public key are present (e.g. .sb traces deleted).

stepback/autorecord.py L33-35 docstring claim 'Patches are reverted on context-manager exit so a Python REPL session can enable() and disable() repeatedly without leaking state.' GROUNDING row 72 only pins enable() signature and active()==False at import. No row demonstrates that after enable()/disable() cycles the openai/anthropic/langchain attributes are restored to their pre-enable identity (id() equality) and active() returns False between cycles.

stepback/trace_diff.py L31-43 docstring claims the algorithm classifies pairs into six statuses: identical, outputs_differ, inputs_differ, kind_differ, a_only, b_only, with the divergence point being the first non-identical pair. GROUNDING row 69 only checks the all-identical fixture (12/12 identical, divergence=None). No GROUNDING row demonstrates outputs_differ, inputs_differ, kind_differ, a_only, or b_only being correctly emitted on divergent fixtures, nor that divergence_step equals the index of the first non-identical pair.

README §7 / autorecord.py L8 advertises `stepback record --output trace.sb -- python my_agent.py` records an UNMODIFIED agent script via the process-global ambient recorder + monkeypatched openai/anthropic/langchain clients. GROUNDING row 67 only checks `record` appears in --help; row 72 only pins enable() signature. No GROUNDING row runs the CLI on an unmodified third-party-style script that calls openai/anthropic and shows the resulting .sb trace contains the expected llm_call frames.

stepback/cli.py `attest` and `verify-pack` subcommands form an end-to-end attestation flow: `stepback attest TRACE -o pack` then `stepback verify-pack pack` exits 0 and reports verify=ok. GROUNDING row 67 only checks both subcommands appear in --help. Row 68 exercises the Python API (build_attestation_pack/write_attestation_pack/verify_attestation_pack) but no GROUNDING row runs the CLI flow itself.

stepback/cli.py `trace-diff` subcommand: README and row 67 advertise it as one of the new subcommands. GROUNDING row 67 only checks --help; row 69 exercises the Python API diff_traces+render_trace_diff. No GROUNDING row runs `stepback trace-diff a.sb b.sb --format markdown -o report.md` and shows the produced file is a >1KB markdown document starting with `#`, nor that the CLI exits non-zero on divergence (a CLI behaviour test_cli_trace_diff_exit_nonzero_on_divergence pins but is not grounded).

stepback/attestation.py docstring claim that the pack body_hash is a sha256 over canonical JSON and that body tampering after signing is detected by verify_attestation_pack (test_tampered_pack_body_fails_verification exists). GROUNDING row 68 only emits the happy-path verify=ok output. No row pins that mutating one byte of the entries array (or summary) inside an already-signed pack causes verify_attestation_pack to raise AttestationVerificationError.

stepback/attestation.py summary aggregation claim (L240-247): summary.replayed_ok counts entries with replay_status=='ok', summary.divergent_traces counts entries with divergent_step_count>0, summary.verified_ok counts entries that passed HMAC+signature verification. No GROUNDING row emits a summary on a known-mixed corpus (e.g. one corrupt trace + one diverging substitution + one clean) and asserts the four counters take the expected non-trivial values; row 68 has trace_count=1, verified_ok=1, divergent_traces=0, so the aggregation logic is exercised only on a degenerate single-clean-entry corpus.

stepback/minimize.py L24-27 docstring: 'results are memoised by canonical subset key (sorted item ids plus the frozen excluded set), so strategies that revisit the same subset don't re-pay the replay'. GROUNDING row 86 only exercises a single ddmin run with probes=3; no row demonstrates the cache hit (e.g. brute-force with intentional re-visits running fewer probes than 2^n - 1, or a probe counter that does NOT advance on a memoised lookup).

stepback/minimize.py MinimizeOptions: 'time_budget_s' wall-clock bound and 'progress' callback. No GROUNDING row triggers the time budget (test that a long predicate aborts with BudgetExhausted after time_budget_s elapses) or pins that the progress callable is invoked once per probe with (probes_so_far, current_size). Row 86 only pins ddmin happy-path output.

stepback/minimize.py BudgetExhausted: docstring L31-32 claims it is raised 'carrying the partial result'. No GROUNDING row constructs a probe_budget=1 ddmin call on a >1-element non-trivial set and asserts the raised BudgetExhausted exposes a partial MinimizationResult attribute (or equivalent) with the best-so-far minimal subset.

stepback/minimize.py ShapleyAttributionStrategy: docstring L20-22 claims it 'returns weights per substitution in addition to the 1-minimal subset'. GROUNDING row 85 only verifies the strategy name string 'shapley' is exposed. No row exercises a 3-element fixture, calls attribute_substitutions, and asserts the per-substitution Shapley weights sum to ~1.0 (or that the singleton-blame fixture concentrates ~1.0 on the responsible item).

stepback/minimize.py find_all_minimal: docstring L34-36 claims it enumerates 'disjoint witnesses' via the 'excluded' option. No GROUNDING row constructs a fixture with TWO disjoint causes (e.g. subs A and B independently flip the predicate when applied alone) and asserts find_all_minimal returns BOTH [A] and [B] as separate witnesses.

stepback/policy_audit.py docstring L23-31 four-status step classification (unchanged / divergent / newly_blocked / newly_allowed). GROUNDING row 88 only exercises the all-unchanged path on 3 clean traces (divergent=0, newly_blocked=0). No GROUNDING row demonstrates a fixture where audit_policy_change returns a TraceImpact with divergent>0, newly_blocked>0, AND newly_allowed>0, so 3 of the 4 status arms are exercised only by tests, not by GROUNDING.

stepback/policy_audit.py docstring L49-52 claim: 'renderers are intentionally pure functions of the report data ... two engineers running the same audit get byte-identical Markdown'. No GROUNDING row constructs a report twice from the same inputs and asserts to_markdown() and to_json_str() return BYTE-IDENTICAL output across the two calls (or across two processes).

stepback/policy_audit.py audit_policy_change(hmac_key=...) HMAC verification: row 82 mentions 'HMAC verification path' as a covered test, but no GROUNDING row demonstrates that audit_policy_change called with the WRONG hmac_key on an HMAC-signed trace raises a verification error (or marks the trace as verified_fail in the report).

stepback/cli.py 'minimize' subcommand: GROUNDING row 93 only counts that 'minimize' appears in --help. No row runs an end-to-end CLI invocation `python -m stepback.cli minimize TRACE --strategy ddmin --predicate ... --probe-budget N` against a fixture trace and asserts (a) exit 0, (b) stdout reports the minimal subset ids, (c) probe-budget exhaustion exits non-zero. The five --strategy values are unverified end-to-end.

stepback/cli.py 'policy-audit' subcommand: GROUNDING row 93 only counts that 'policy-audit' appears in --help. No row runs `python -m stepback.cli policy-audit TRACES... --policy-path P --format markdown --exit-nonzero-on-divergence -o report.md` and asserts (a) exit 0 on no-divergence, (b) exit non-zero on divergence, (c) report.md exists and starts with '#'.

stepback/shims.py wrap_bedrock / bedrock_executor / WrappedBedrock public API: only canonical_bedrock_model_id is grounded (row 92). No GROUNDING row demonstrates wrap_bedrock(client) producing a WrappedBedrock instance whose .converse(...) call records an llm_call frame with the right modelId and rolled-up cost via bedrock_executor in a replay round-trip.

tests/test_substitutions_new.py::test_message_patch_preserves_list_size_on_replace asserts that MessagePatchSubstitution preserves list size. The test passes, but it does not exercise out-of-bounds index behaviour or empty-message-list edge cases — only the happy path is covered, while the test name implies a stronger invariant.

tests/test_jsonpatch.py::test_copy_does_not_share_reference asserts apply_patch performs deep copy on the 'copy' op. Test passes; deep-copy non-aliasing is grounded for one nested-list shape but not asserted across other container kinds (dict-of-dict, list-of-dicts).
is_policy_blocked recognises the third docstring shape: a free-form dict with `blocked: True` and a `reason`/`policy`/`policy_id`/`policy_path` field (stepback/policy_audit.py L80-103)

audit_policy_change actually classifies a step as `newly_blocked` (and increments total_newly_blocked_steps) when the replayed output is policy-denied AND the baseline output was not — GROUNDING row 88 only exercises the trivial 0-divergence path
audit_policy_change classifies a step as `newly_allowed` (baseline blocked, replayed allowed) and the count surfaces in TraceImpact/PolicyImpactReport

The five strategies (DDMin, LinearShrink, BinaryHalving, BruteForce, Shapley) all return the same minimal subset on a fixture with a single guilty substitution — GROUNDING row 85 only verifies they exist by name and row 86 only exercises ddmin

GROUNDING row 107 only exercises 4 of 5 severity classes (identical/equivalent/semantic/structural); MINOR is never demonstrated end-to-end.
